thread.title: Mid-Day Update: Dow Catapulted By Upbeat Results From Boeing and Apple

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day Update: Dow Catapulted By Upbeat Results From Boeing and Apple
text:
Shutterstock photo Buoyed by favorable quarterly results from Dow component stocks Apple ( AAPL ) and Boeing ( BA ), the blue chip index raced higher at Wednesday's open to gain more than 300 points above Tuesday's close. All 11 sectors of the S&P 500 were in the green, while sizable gains in networking and storage stocks lifted the tech-laden Nasdaq by almost 1%.
Stock futures were already off to a strong start on the back of Apple's ( AAPL ) results, but were catapulted higher on the release of Boeing's strong fourth-quarter results that included annual sales that topped $100 billion for the first time in the company's 102-year history, and upbeat guidance that soothed investors' jitters about slowing global growth.
Wednesday's bullish price action was amplified by expectations for the Federal Open Market Committee to keep interest rates unchanged and adopt a less restrictive policy bias, and the commencement of trade talks in Washington between the US and China. High level officials including President Donald Trump and Chinese Vice Premier Liu He are expected to participate in this round of talks.
In other earnings news, AT&T ( T ) missed sales estimates bu t report ed earnings that were in-line with expectations; Ebay ( EBAY ) beat on both EPS and revenue estimates; and McDonald's ( MCD ) reported mixed results but issued upbeat sales growth and earnings targets.
Economic data was mixed as the private sector added 213,000 new jobs, but the housing market continued to decay as pending home sales plummeted 2.2% last month. Year-over-year, pending home sales slid 9.5% compared with December 2017.
With focus shifting to US/China trade talks, European bourses were mostly higher with the UK's FTSE-100 leading advancers thanks to a slightly weaker pound, and progress toward a Brexit deal. The German DAX closed lower as recent data showed inflation running below the European Central Bank's 2% target as well as allegations of money laundering at the Asian unit of Wirecard.
Crude oil was up $1.56 to $54.87 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.01 to $2.89 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $0.70 to $1,315.90 an ounce, while silver was up $0.08 to $15.93 an ounce. Copper was up $0.04 to $2.76 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 3.11% to $11.51 with the United States Natural Gas Fund down 0.43% to $25.74. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.26% to 21.93 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.06% to $123.90. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.40% to $14.94.
